Parallel grammatical structure pattern: each sentence pairs two coordinated clauses with matching verb phrases ("checked the document and updated the record," "wrote the report and signed the official document").

The "either...or" construction establishes a template where the second clause mirrors the first, with a different subject performing a different but parallel action in a different domain.

Final fragment "the engineer inspected the control panel and adjusted the safety system" is an incomplete coordinated clause mid-sentence, strongly expecting continuation with another coordinated action or a concluding phrase (e.g., "to ensure..." or "the safety protocol").
"Then the engineer worked on a different task: he examined the code, checked the control parameters and adjusted the protection system" — a new domain shift suggesting continuation with another technical action or object phrase.
"adjusted the protection system" ends mid-thought.
